title: 5.4.6 Plain English to Pseudocode: A Method That Calls a Method
description: Turn five plain-English steps into pseudocode: one decision, two calls to other methods, and a step that runs either way.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([takeDamage starts]) --> B[take the damage off health]
  B --> C{health zero or less?}
  C -- yes --> D[[die]]
  C -- no --> E[[flashRed]]
  D --> E
  E --> F([back to the caller])
planChart.caption: takeDamage: the die call sits on one branch, and both branches reach flashRed.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** The enemy is hit for some amount of damage.

**2.** Take that amount off the enemy's health.

**3.** If the health is now zero or less, the enemy dies.

**4.** Either way, the enemy flashes red to show it was hit.

**5.** Then control goes back to whoever hit it.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the five steps.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Use SET for a change, IF and END IF for a decision, and CALL for another method. The two methods here are named `die` and `flashRed`. Number every line, including the indented one and END IF. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `SET score TO score + 10` (a change)
- `IF lives <= 0` ... `END IF` (a decision; indent what is inside it)
- `CALL playSound` (call another method; `CALL this.playSound` is fine too)

The chart shows the shape.
hints: A step that happens "either way" is not inside the IF. It comes after END IF.
Write a call as one line, like `CALL playSound`. Do not write what die does.

requirements.title: Five numbered steps in a row
requirements.description: Number every step 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: You need at least five lines that start with a number, one after another, each with a step written after it.

requirements.title: The damage comes off health first
requirements.description: Health goes down by the damage, before the decision.
requirements.hint: Change health by the damage amount, and put that step before the IF.

requirements.title: One decision about health being zero or less
requirements.description: Exactly one IF, about health and zero, closed with END IF.
requirements.hint: Use one IF that asks if health is zero or less, and close it with END IF. If you have two IFs, join them into one.

requirements.title: The enemy only dies inside the decision
requirements.description: The call to die sits inside the decision.
requirements.hint: The enemy only dies when health is zero or less, so the call to die goes inside the decision.

requirements.title: The flash happens either way
requirements.description: The flash runs whether or not the enemy died, so it sits outside the decision.
requirements.hint: Step 4 says "either way". A step that runs either way is not inside the decision: put it after END IF.

requirements.title: Exactly two calls
requirements.description: One call for die and one for flashRed. Do not write what those methods do.
requirements.hint: You need exactly two CALL lines, one for die and one for flashRed. What die does belongs inside die, not here.
